fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "A Book Written for the Elevator Ride", "body": "Jorge says World War You was built to be a short whirlwind tour, written as if he were talking to a stranger on an elevator and trying to say as much as he could before the ride ended. He wanted newcomers to avoid feeling overwhelmed and longtime researchers to avoid feeling bored, so he leaves crumbs instead of conclusions and quotes figures like Miles Davis and Johannes Kepler. Chance, who read it in one sitting, says fact smacking people rarely works, while Gabe compares the approach to Sam Tripoli's rule of the ronin, where you wait to be asked."}, {"title": "Dasein and the Three Worlds Under Attack", "body": "Chance frames worldview warfare through Heidegger's Dasein, being in the world, which he splits into three parts: the Eigenwelt or inner world, the Umwelt or natural world, and the Mitwelt or social world. He argues a person can shrug off attacks on the inner self, but if they come to believe the world is doomed or society is monstrous, their own growth is quietly sabotaged, and he ties this to how he reads the biofield. Chance also embraces a checkers metaphor raised in the conversation, where the old compulsory jump rule lets a player lure an opponent into traps, and links it to victims who become perpetrators."}, {"title": "Dinosaurs, Godzilla and Catching You Young", "body": "Jorge argues that dinosaurs belong in the same category as outer space imagery, pushed relentlessly at children until a kid's first four syllable word is triceratops, and he questions how bones alone reveal feathers. Chance reads the extinction story as eschatology telling humans they are next, while Gabe calls the theory of evolution a magnified retelling of life in the womb. A self described Godzilla nerd, Jorge walks through the series from 1954, pointing to its nuclear themes, a United Nations weather control plot, and a VHS cover showing monsters atop the Twin Towers."}, {"title": "Perpetual Motion and the Straw Man", "body": "Chance highlights the book's claim that a perpetual motion machine cannot be patented, along with a 1940 Rube Goldberg cartoon called Something for Nothing that he says taught audiences why engines need fuel. He argues the impossibility claim is a straw man, since nobody sensible expects a machine that never needs a push or repairs, and points to water wheels and the moving heavens as continual motion. Gabe connects the same era to Prohibition, saying it kept people from making their own alcohol fuel while patents were streamlined toward Rockefeller pipelines."}, {"title": "Two Kinds of Balance and the Use of Evil", "body": "Returning to the adjustment card from his Loki streams with Gabe, Chance describes two kinds of equilibrium: a static balance of opposites that cancels manifestation, which he calls an inverted Gnostic path, and a living balance like the water cycle, always moving and always fair. From there he offers his answer to why evil exists. Those aligned with life allow others freedom, that freedom permits harm, and the resulting trials sharpen the good, much like a tomato plant needs wind to grow strong. Jorge adds that modern messaging sells childlessness as freedom."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Vibe Rant regular Jorge Mesa of Third Eye Edify returns tonight to talk about his brand new book, World War You, a deep dive into the diverse and devious deceptions that have been weaponized for use on the first and last frontier of human conflict, the mind. Tying together a tremendous quantity of topics, including dinosaurs, Hollywood, video games, ad campaigns, shadow figures and the robotization of mankind, we'll be taking the fight to the only place that can make a real difference: our world-view.
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "I wrote it like I was talking to somebody on an elevator, I guess, some random person I had just met and I tried to say as much as I can before the elevator ride was over.", "author": "Jorge Mesa", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/b6c1cc31-295a-4776-830c-de5410a896c0/JORGE-MESA.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "What have these entertainments that we've traded authentic human experiences for? And they got you.", "author": "Jorge Mesa", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/b6c1cc31-295a-4776-830c-de5410a896c0/JORGE-MESA.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The theory of evolution is nothing more than a hyperbolic derivative of the embryo in the zygote and coming into this world.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "And it's been marketed towards children no matter what the whole time, whether it's a pretty sinister movie or whether Godzilla's good or bad. It's in convincing us that they can do stuff.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "You have to be able to imagine something for it to be possible or for it to exist in your universe.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "And so now I'm looking at those personality types as angelic orientations as these three different groups in the Enneagram, that's very useful.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "The key crux of all this is the belief that it's a need, believe that you can't do without it. We think that they're names, but I think they're actually thought forms.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "The evil in its freedom, granted to it by the good, strengthens the good, and everything that's seemingly decay and evil, just like in winter, the plants that die create room for new and stronger and better plants to come up later.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
